v1.feedback: Diaphanous clearly drove material choices — ghostly sphere opacity, dissolving thread ends, drape-curtain rule, pale lavender palette — but the mutation is almost entirely tonal rather than structural; the parent skeleton (ring anchors, convergence/proximity/span rules) is unchanged, so this reads more like a color-grade pass than a morph. A refined version should let the word reshape geometry too: taper thread density so the upper hemisphere is dense gauze while lower threads thin to near-nothing, or add per-line opacity falloff along length so strands visibly dissolve rather than just being uniformly pale. The sphere's triple-layer glow (mesh + inner + halo) is a nice touch but at these opacities it may vanish entirely on dim monitors — test with gamma 2.4.

v2.feedback: The diaphanous concept genuinely drives structural changes — height-based density culling, per-vertex dissolve alpha, veil curtain panels — rather than just renaming variables, and the parent Shiota-room form is clearly preserved. However, the room dimensions (42×34×46) relative to SPHERE_R=1.8 risk making the sphere read as a tiny ornament in a vast dark void; tighten the room or push the camera closer (orbit radius ~14 instead of ~24) so the gauze canopy fills more frame. The veil curtain panels feel bolted-on rather than organically grown from the parent's radial thread logic — consider instead modulating the existing anchor density with a fabric-drape displacement field so the diaphanous quality emerges from the same generative system rather than a separate anchor loop.
